question: Why Is My Shipping Rate Showing in the Wrong Currency?
metaDescription: Usually a live-rate carrier plugin returning its own default currency, a multi-currency plugin not converting shipping costs, or a hardcoded rate value.
shortAnswer: A shipping rate displaying in the wrong currency is typically caused by a live-rate carrier plugin returning a cost in its own default or account currency without converting it to the store's configured currency, a multi-currency plugin converting product prices but not applying the same conversion to shipping costs, or a manually configured Flat Rate cost that was entered assuming a different currency than the store actually uses.

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

Currency handling for shipping costs generally isn't automatic across every plugin — core WooCommerce's own shipping methods use whatever currency the store is configured for by default, but a live-rate carrier integration querying an external API may return values in a currency tied to the connected carrier account rather than the store's storefront currency, requiring an explicit conversion step that isn't always handled correctly out of the box.

Common Causes

  • A live carrier-rate plugin returning costs in the currency of the connected shipping account rather than converting to the store's display currency.
  • A multi-currency plugin converting product prices correctly but missing shipping cost conversion, a common gap depending on the specific plugin's implementation.
  • A Flat Rate cost entered manually in the wrong currency by mistake, especially after a store's default currency was changed at some point without revisiting existing shipping method costs.
  • Currency symbol display settings being separate from the actual currency the calculation is performed in, occasionally creating a mismatch between what's shown and what's actually charged.

How to Fix It

  1. Confirm the store's actual default currency setting under Settings → General.
  2. Check whether a multi-currency plugin's conversion covers shipping costs, not just product prices.
  3. Review any live-rate carrier plugin's currency configuration, ensuring it converts to the store's display currency correctly.
  4. Re-verify manually entered Flat Rate costs after any currency change to the store.
